title: Two Oscillators, a Radio and a Reset
summary: Make slow and fast oscillators, send a tone to an AM radio, rebuild the 4040 drummer with a reset, and starve it of power for glitches.

subs.text: Connect the power rails on both sides with two jumpers at the right end of the breadboard.
Place the 40106 chip across the center gap, then add its power and ground jumpers.
Add a trimmer (a small knob) next to the chip and two short red jumpers below it.
Add the large capacitor at the bottom left. A big capacitor makes the oscillator slow.
Add a long jumper from the top rail to the middle of the board, and a yellow jumper below it.
Insert the audio jack.
Clip the battery connector onto the 9V battery.
Plug the battery wires into the top power rail.
Plug the audio cable into the jack.
Add a resistor from the oscillator's output to the yellow jumper, and listen to the slow pulse.
Remove the output resistor.
Add a second trimmer at the top, with two short red jumpers to the chip.
Add a second large capacitor at the top left. Now there are two slow oscillators.
Add two resistors, one from each oscillator, to the yellow jumper to mix them.
Take the two resistors out again.
Put two diodes in their place. Diodes combine the oscillators in a different way.
Remove both large capacitors.
Add two small capacitors in their places. Both oscillators now sing as tones, like the Blade Runner soundtrack.
Unplug the audio cable.
Remove the audio jack and its two jumpers.
Remove the two diodes.
Connect a long, thin wire to the oscillator's output. It works as an antenna.
Lay the antenna wire along the board.
Swap the lower capacitor for a tiny one, so the oscillator runs at radio frequency.
Hold an AM radio near the board and turn the trimmer until you hear it on the radio.
Put the radio away and remove the antenna and the small capacitors.
Put the two large capacitors back: two slow oscillators again.
Place the 4040 counter chip in the middle and add its power and ground jumpers.
Add a short red jumper from the top rail to the 4040's top row.
Run a long orange wire from the first oscillator's output to the 4040's clock input.
Add a short red jumper at the bottom right for the jack's signal, then a jumper from the top rail for the jack's ground.
Insert the audio jack and plug in the cable.
Add a resistor and a diode from the 4040's outputs to the jack.
Add another diode and a small capacitor, then turn the trimmer to change the tempo.
Remove the short red jumper above the 4040.
Connect the second oscillator's output to the 4040's reset pin. Now the second oscillator restarts the pattern.
Add a second small capacitor next to the first. Turn both trimmers to find patterns you like. An LED from the jack's signal row to ground shows the rhythm.
Take the LED out and listen to the finished drummer with reset.
Unplug the battery's red (+) wire.
Add a short jumper from the + rail at the right end.
Add a trimmer and plug the red wire into it, so all the power passes through the knob. Turn it slowly to starve the circuit of voltage and hear it glitch.
